m_dialogEntries.m_dialog: AAAAHHHH! No, don't eat my face! Oh, Wizard! Stop messing around and tell me what happened at the Gravulum Order Lab!
Angry Treants, you say? Uh huh... protecting their tree brethren? Well, that explains some things. What exactly those things are, I'm not sure!
But when I do, you'll be the first to know! Until then. Bye!
<ITALICS>Well, now this reading is... interesting. Your Badge doesn't have spilt food or some other weird combat-related shrapnel on it does it? </ITALICS>
<ITALICS>No? Hmm. Then I'm going to need you to go to the super secret Gravulum Order Lab in Marleybone and inspect the Spiral Pekronometer. Thanks! </ITALICS>
<ITALICS>Wizard! Your Badge is sending all sorts of erratic readings. Get to work on the Pekronometer! </ITALICS>
<ITALICS>Huzzah! The atmospheric Pekron readings have stabilized! You fixed the Pekronometer, eh? Great work! </ITALICS>
<ITALICS>Now, make like a tree and hustle back and give me the full report! </ITALICS>
Go away! I don't have time for your Drama Club bake sale or whatever nonsense you're- Oh, you're you! Glad you've come. We've got work to do...
I've discovered discrepancies between the results of your Pekron readings versus those collected by my Wide-Range Spiral Pekronometer.
What's a Wide-Range Spiral Pekronometer? Why, it's a device that reads Pekron levels over the entire wide range of the Spiral!
What do you mean, why do I need your readings if there's already a machine that does it? Because even pseudo-science requires confirmation!
Can you collect an environmental Pekron reading in the Wizard City Dye Shop? That should be the only reading I'll need today. Probably. Maybe.
